_note: Curated PHRASE FRAMES for the narrative_detail support tier (research/dossier.py). Where narrative_entities.json holds names, this holds the frames that make a sentence tell you where something CAME FROM or what HAPPENED. Amend it the way you amend moments.json.
_never_a_hook: narrative_detail is NOT in HOOKABLE_TAGS and never will be. Everything listed here can only affect what SUPPORTS a lead, never what opens one.
_matching: CASE-INSENSITIVE, word-bounded at the start of the phrase (so 'debut' also catches 'debuted', 'debuts'). These are ordinary verbs and prepositions, not proper nouns, so case carries no information.
_seeded: 2026-09-12 — derived from the 735 spec facts across 250 dossiers.
_provenance_note: Phrases here are ORIGIN and EVENT frames. Two that look like they belong and do not: 'heritage' and 'vintage' — both are GOAT materials boilerplate ('Heritage details include a perforated toe box'), and adding either pulls in pure spec copy.
_placement_note: THE EXCLUSION, and the reason the tier has any precision at all. A sentence can name Supreme, Cactus Jack and Levi's and still be pure materials copy, because the entity is a LOGO SITTING ON A PART OF THE SHOE: 'a rubberized Cactus Jack patch adorns the tongue'. A sentence whose only signal is an entity inside one of these frames STAYS SPEC. A provenance marker overrides the exclusion — "a '94' embroidered on the lateral heel — a nod to Supreme's founding year" is placement AND provenance, and the provenance is the part worth telling. 54 of the 146 entity/provenance hits are held back here.
